audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Shunammite restoration, Hazael oracle, and Judah/Israel royal transition narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for famine migration, land-restoration petition, Gehazi's testimony, royal restitution, Ben-hadad's illness, Hazael's deception and killing, Elisha's tears over future atrocities, Jehoram and Ahaziah chronology, dynastic intermarriage, Edomite revolt, and war injury.

verses.restored: Elisha spoke to woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, Rise and go, you and your household, and sojourn wherever you can sojourn, for YHWH has called for famine, and it is also coming upon land seven years.
The woman rose and did according to word of man of Divine; she went, she and her household, and sojourned in land of Philistines seven years.
It was at end of seven years that woman returned from land of Philistines and went out to cry to king for her house and her field.
King was speaking to Gehazi servant of man of Divine, saying, Recount to me, please, all great things Elisha has done.

It was, as he was recounting to king how he restored dead one to life, that look, woman whose son he restored to life cried to king for her house and field. Gehazi said, My lord king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life.
King asked woman, and she recounted to him. King appointed to her one officer, saying, Restore all belonging to her and all produce of field from day she left land until now.
Elisha came to Damascus, and Ben-hadad king of Aram was sick. It was told to him, saying, Man of Divine has come here.
King said to Hazael, Take a gift in your hand and go to meet man of Divine, and inquire of YHWH through him, saying, Shall I recover from this sickness?

Hazael went to meet him and took gift in his hand, every good thing of Damascus, burden of forty camels. He came and stood before him and said, Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram sent me to you, saying, Shall I recover from this sickness?
Elisha said to him, Go, say to him, Recovering, you shall recover; yet YHWH has shown me that dying, he shall die.
He fixed his face and set it until shame, and man of Divine wept.

Hazael said, Why is my lord weeping? He said, Because I know evil you will do to children of Israel: their fortified places you will send into fire, their young men you will kill by sword, their little ones you will dash, and their pregnant women you will rip open.
Hazael said, But what is your servant, the dog, that he should do this great thing? Elisha said, YHWH has shown me you as king over Aram.
He went from Elisha and came to his lord. He said to him, What did Elisha say to you? He said, He told me, Recovering, you shall recover.
It was on next day that he took coverlet, dipped it in water, spread it over his face, and he died. Hazael reigned in his place.
In fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign.
Thirty-two years old was he when he became king, and eight years he reigned in Jerusalem.
He walked in way of kings of Israel, as house of Ahab did, for daughter of Ahab was his wife; he did evil in eyes of YHWH.
Yet YHWH was unwilling to destroy Judah for sake of David his servant, as he had spoken to give him a lamp for his sons all days.
In his days Edom revolted from under hand of Judah and made a king over themselves.
Joram crossed to Zair, and all chariots with him. He rose by night and struck Edomites surrounding him and commanders of chariots, but people fled to their tents.
Edom revolted from under hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah revolted at that time.
Remaining matters of Joram and all he did, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Judah?
Joram lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in city of David; Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
In twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah began to reign.
Twenty-two years old was Ahaziah when he became king, and one year he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Athaliah daughter/granddaughter of Omri king of Israel.
He walked in way of house of Ahab and did evil in eyes of YHWH like house of Ahab, for he was son-in-law of house of Ahab.
He went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and Arameans struck Joram.

King Joram returned to be healed at Jezreel from wounds Arameans struck him at Ramah when he fought Hazael king of Aram. Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram son of Ahab at Jezreel because he was sick/wounded.

translation_notes: The Shunammite woman migrates with her household because of famine and later petitions for restoration of house, field, and accumulated produce. Displacement does not erase property claims.
Her case is heard directly, verified, and remedied with back produce. This is restitution, not charity.
Gehazi's appearance after chapter 5 creates chronological and compositional questions, especially if his skin disease is assumed continuous; the text should not force a simplistic timeline.
Ben-hadad's sickness is not moral failure. The danger lies in succession politics and Hazael's actions, not illness itself.
Elisha's statement to Hazael is textually and morally difficult: the king may recover from the illness but will still die. Hazael reports only the reassuring half.
Elisha weeps before naming Hazael's future atrocities. Prophetic knowledge does not equal approval, and foreknowledge does not remove Hazael's responsibility.
The listed atrocities include burning cities, killing young men, dashing children, and ripping open pregnant women. These are war crimes and must never be sanctified by prophecy.
Hazael's 'dog' language is self-abasement and disbelief, not permission to dehumanize people through animal comparisons.
Hazael kills Ben-hadad by suffocation with a wet coverlet. The narrative must not become instruction or apologetics for political assassination.
Royal marriage connections are narrated as dynastic influence, but women such as Athaliah and Ahab's daughter must not be made scapegoats for men's policies.
Edom's revolt is a subject people's political break from Judah; imperial loss is not automatically moral chaos.
Regnal synchronisms and Athaliah's relation to Omri vary in interpretation and require textual-chronological audit.
safety_note: Do not blame famine migrants, erase displaced owners, stigmatize illness, glorify assassination, or treat prophecy as approval of atrocity. Preserve the Shunammite woman's right to full restitution, Elisha's grief, Hazael's accountability, the humanity of Edomites and Arameans, and the moral horror of violence against children and pregnant people.
